chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Kufi al-Qurashi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from someone who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Maymun, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: If one of you performs Hajj a thousand times, but does not visit the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he has left a right among the rights of Allah, the Exalted. And when asked about that, he said: The right of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is obligatory upon every Muslim.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) declaring that the Ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) is a fundamental right of Allah (Haqq Allah) obligatory upon every Muslim, regardless of their gender or status. This narration elevates the visitation from a recommended act to a mandatory duty, emphasizing that neglecting it renders even a thousand Hajj pilgrimages incomplete, as the spiritual connection to the Ahl al-Bayt is central to Islamic devotion.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz Al-Kūfi Al-Qurashi narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from someone who narrated to him, from ‘Ali ibn Maymūn, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Verily if one of you goes for Hajj one thousand times but does not go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.), he has neglected one of his obligations toward Allāh, the Exalted. Then someone asked the Imam (a.s.) for the reason and he replied, “Fulfilling one’s obligation toward Ḥusain (a.s.) is mandatory on every Muslim.”
